question: What is the main goal of medical asepsis in the ward?

options.D: To reduce the number of germs

explanation: Medical asepsis is all about cutting down the number of germs and stopping them from spreading. Surgical asepsis, on the other hand, aims for complete sterility. You're doing great!

question: When must you clean your hands when wearing gloves?

options.A: Only when the gloves look dirty or torn
options.B: After removing them, but never before
options.C: Before putting them on and after taking them off
options.D: Only before putting on a fresh pair

explanation: Always wash or sanitize your hands before donning gloves and right after doffing them! Gloves can get tiny tears, and your hands can easily pick up germs during removal.

question: Which routine nursing task calls for clean examination gloves?

options.A: Measuring a patient's resting blood pressure
options.B: Handing a clean meal tray to a patient
options.D: Emptying a urinary catheter drainage bag

explanation: Urine is a body fluid, so you definitely want glove protection to avoid exposure when emptying that drainage bag. Simple and safe!

question: You are about to check the oral temperature of a patient whose skin is intact. What should you do about gloves?

options.A: Skip gloves because skin is intact and no fluids are expected
options.B: Wear standard examination gloves just in case

explanation: For routine checks involving unbroken skin and no body fluids, gloves aren't needed. This saves precious hospital supplies and time!

question: What is a major difference between standard examination gloves and surgical gloves?

options.A: Surgical gloves are strictly sterile and have longer cuffs
options.B: Examination gloves are always thicker and tougher
options.C: Examination gloves come in precise numbered hand sizes
options.D: Surgical gloves are only used for drawing blood

explanation: Surgical gloves are sterile and feature longer cuffs to cover your gown sleeves, keeping the operating field completely germ-free.

question: When should you choose sterile surgical gloves instead of regular exam gloves?

options.A: When performing a procedure inside a sterile body cavity
options.B: During routine physical checks on unbroken skin
options.C: Whenever touching a patient with an infection
options.D: When cleaning up a blood spill on the floor

explanation: Whenever you enter a sterile space or use sterile instruments, you need sterile gloves to keep bacteria out. You've got this!

question: Which glove material gives you a great feel (tactile sensitivity) but can cause nasty allergies?
explanation: Natural rubber latex fits like a second skin, but protein allergies make it a risk for both healthcare workers and patients.

question: You need cheap gloves for quick, low-risk tasks where tearing isn't a big worry. Which material is best?
explanation: Vinyl is budget-friendly and latex-free, making it ideal for quick, low-risk chores where you don't need heavy-duty strength.

question: What is the very first thing you must do before putting on examination gloves?
explanation: Always clean your hands first! Putting gloves on unwashed hands traps germs right against your skin.

question: Why does wearing the correct glove size matter so much in clinical work?

options.A: It prevents tearing and keeps your fingers nimble
options.B: It stops the material from causing latex allergies
options.C: It keeps the gloves completely sterile
options.D: It means you don't have to wash your hands afterwards

explanation: Gloves that are too tight will easily rip, while oversized gloves make it hard to grip things. Finding your right size is key!

question: When taking off dirty gloves, where should your very first move begin?

options.A: Tearing the palm area to loosen a tight fit
options.C: Grasping the outside of the cuff and peeling downward
options.D: Snapping the wristband outward with a quick flick

explanation: Pinching the outer cuff lets you peel the glove inside out, trapping all the nasty germs safely on the inside.

question: Why do you hold the first removed glove inside the palm of your remaining gloved hand?

options.A: To stop the latex from releasing powder into the air
options.B: To easily peel off the second glove without touching its dirty outside
options.C: To keep the first glove clean so you can use it again
options.D: To save space in the waste bin

explanation: Ball up the first glove in your palm so your bare fingers can safely slide under the clean inner cuff of the second glove. Clever and safe!

question: Which of these is a dangerous and incorrect practice with disposable medical gloves?

options.A: Cleaning your hands before putting them on
options.C: Washing and reusing them between patients
options.D: Changing them after every single patient

explanation: Disposable gloves are strictly single-use! Washing them ruins their protective barrier and spreads germs around the ward.

question: Which situation is an example of cross-contamination from poor glove habits?

options.A: Not wearing gloves to take a pulse on an arm
options.B: Touching a computer keyboard with gloves you wore during wound care
options.C: Washing your hands right after taking off both gloves
options.D: Choosing a larger glove size to avoid thumb tears

explanation: Using dirty gloves on shared equipment like keyboards transfers patient germs to surfaces where other staff can pick them up.

question: Under standard precautions, when should a nurse wear gloves?

options.A: Whenever you give oral medications to older adults
options.B: Whenever there is a chance of touching blood or body fluids
options.C: During every single interaction with any patient
options.D: Only when caring for patients in isolation rooms

explanation: Standard precautions apply to everyone. If you expect contact with moist body substances, glove up!

question: A patient is in contact precautions for a resistant bug. What is the rule for gloves in this room?

options.A: Wear gloves only if the patient is bleeding
options.B: Keep the same pair on for your whole shift
options.C: Put on gloves before entering the room and remove them before leaving
options.D: Wear gloves only if doing a surgical dressing change

explanation: For contact precautions, put on your gloves right before you step into the room, and take them off before you step out to contain the germs.
